title: Capture enough observations during the incident to diagnose later while focusing on getting the system back running
summary: During a P1 incident, support should prioritize restoring operation and, in parallel, capture enough observable evidence for later diagnosis—rather than attempting full root-cause determination in real time.
when_to_use: Use during a high-severity (P1) incident when the system is not running and you need to both (1) restore operation quickly and (2) collect sufficient observations for later diagnosis.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Lead the call flow to (a) check RMS for system faults first and (b) coordinate with the operator to capture Aviva-observable information when direct Aviva access is not available.
Operator (site): Provide screen/observations from Aviva/HMI when requested by L1_support, since L1_support may not have direct Aviva access.
access_or_tools_needed: WCS/OptiSweep state visibility (as available via the supported surfaces mentioned in the source)
Operator access for Aviva observations (when direct Aviva access is unavailable)
Support note-taking/ticketing (implied by the source emphasis on capturing notes)

steps.title: Prioritize restoring operation while preparing for later diagnosis
steps.purpose: Ensure the incident response focuses on getting the system back running quickly while still collecting enough evidence for later root-cause work.
steps.instruction: During the call, keep the primary objective on restoring operation (how can we get the system back and running?), and in parallel capture enough observations for later diagnosis.
steps.expected_result: You have a running plan to restore operation and you are actively collecting incident observations (not attempting full 100% diagnosis in real time).
steps.healthy_condition: The call is structured around restoration first, with evidence capture occurring continuously (e.g., RMS faults and cross-system state comparisons).
steps.failure_condition: The team spends time trying to fully diagnose root cause in real time and/or does not capture the minimum observable evidence needed for later diagnosis.

actions.label: Set call objective to restore operation first
actions.exact_action: Focus on restoring operation (source emphasizes 'how can we get the system back and running?').

actions.label: Capture enough notes for later diagnosis
actions.exact_action: Take enough notes so that we can diagnose it later.

steps.title: Check RMS first for system faults
steps.purpose: Establish the first observable evidence point during the call by checking RMS for system faults.
steps.instruction: On the phone call, go to the RMS screen first and check whether there are any system faults.
steps.expected_result: RMS is checked and you have an observable answer to whether RMS shows system faults.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS system faults are reviewed as the first step on the call.
steps.failure_condition: RMS is not checked first, or system faults are not captured as part of the incident notes.

actions.label: Open RMS and check system faults
actions.exact_action: Go to that RMS screen, see if any system faults.

steps.title: Use operator-provided Aviva observations when direct Aviva access is unavailable
steps.purpose: Collect Aviva-side observable information without requiring direct Aviva access by coordinating with the operator to look in Aviva.
steps.instruction: If you do not have access to Aviva, ask the operator to look in Aviva and tell you what they are seeing (so you can capture the Aviva-observable action/status for later diagnosis).
steps.expected_result: You have Aviva-observable information captured via the operator (since direct Aviva access is not available).
steps.healthy_condition: Operator is engaged to provide Aviva observations; the incident notes include what Aviva indicates.
steps.failure_condition: No Aviva observations are captured because Aviva was not checked via the operator when direct access was unavailable.

actions.label: Request operator to check Aviva
actions.exact_action: You have the URL to the dashboard to the... We don't have the access to Aviva... the best thing you will have, you'll have an operator who will... tell you where to look in Aviva to tell you, you know, what they're seeing.

steps.title: Compare Aviva-reported action with WCS/OptiSweep system state
steps.purpose: Determine whether the issue is likely on the Aviva/HMI side or on the communication/system side by comparing what Aviva indicates versus what WCS/OptiSweep shows.
steps.instruction: When there is an issue between OPC and Aviva (or when Aviva triggers an action), check the WCS/OptiSweep state to see whether the system state matches the Aviva-reported action. If Aviva indicates a state change (e.g., startup) but WCS/OptiSweep does not show it, treat it as a communication issue and capture that mismatch as evidence.
steps.expected_result: Your notes include (a) what Aviva indicates and (b) what WCS/OptiSweep state shows, including whether the expected state change is present or missing.
steps.healthy_condition: Aviva action and WCS/OptiSweep state are compared and the match/mismatch is recorded for later diagnosis.
steps.failure_condition: No cross-system comparison is recorded (Aviva vs WCS/OptiSweep), leaving insufficient evidence for later diagnosis.

actions.label: Check WCS/OptiSweep state after Aviva action
actions.exact_action: See in WCS or in our Opti sweep, what is the state of the system.

success_criteria: RMS system faults were checked and recorded as part of the call evidence.
Aviva-observable information was captured via the operator when direct Aviva access was unavailable.
A comparison was recorded between Aviva-indicated action/status and the observed WCS/OptiSweep system state (including any mismatch).
The team focused on restoring operation while collecting sufficient evidence for later diagnosis (not full 100% diagnosis in real time).
healthy_conditions: RMS system faults are reviewed early in the call.
Aviva observations are obtained through the operator when needed.
WCS/OptiSweep state is checked to confirm whether Aviva-indicated actions are reflected in system state.
failure_conditions: RMS system faults were not checked or not recorded.
Aviva observations were not captured (and direct Aviva access was unavailable).
No Aviva vs WCS/OptiSweep state comparison was recorded, preventing later diagnosis.
The incident response attempts full root-cause diagnosis in real time instead of restoring operation under P1 SLA pressure.
escalation_guidance: If the system cannot be brought back running within the SLA pressure described for P1 incidents, escalate (the source frames this as a firefight due to UPS 4-hour SLA on P1s).

If evidence capture is incomplete, later diagnosis may be delayed—ensure at minimum the source-backed evidence points (RMS faults, Aviva observations via operator, and Aviva vs WCS/OptiSweep state match/mismatch) are recorded.

The packet does not provide explicit WCS/OptiSweep UI/API surface names or specific query steps to retrieve the 'state of the system'—only the instruction to check WCS or OptiSweep state.
